title: LLM Prompting Essentials: Tokens, Sampling, Structure and RAG
summary: Quick revision notes on how LLMs read text (tokens, context windows), how sampling settings shape output, how to split system and user prompts, how to force structured JSON, and how to ground answers with retrieved context in RAG prompt templates.

chapters.title: Tokens and Context Windows: The Mental Model
points: A token is a sub-word chunk (about 4 English characters or 0.75 words); the model reads and predicts tokens, never raw characters or words
Context window = input tokens + output tokens combined; exceeding it truncates or errors, and the output budget (max_tokens) is carved out of the same window
Billing, latency and limits are all counted in tokens; output tokens usually cost more than input tokens
Tokenizers differ per model, so the same text gives different token counts; count with the provider's tokenizer, never estimate by word count for limits
Long context is not free attention: details buried in the middle of a long prompt are recalled worse than those at the start or end

chapters.title: Sampling Controls: Temperature and Top-p
points: The model outputs a probability distribution over the next token; sampling settings decide how one token is picked from it
Temperature rescales the distribution: 0 is near-deterministic (greedy), around 0.7 to 1 is varied, above 1 gets erratic
Top-p (nucleus) keeps the smallest set of tokens whose cumulative probability reaches p, e.g. top_p=0.9, then samples within it
Temperature changes how flat the distribution is; top-p changes how many tokens are allowed: tune one, leave the other at default
Use temperature 0 for extraction, classification, code and RAG answers; use higher for brainstorming and creative writing
Example call: client.messages.create(model=..., temperature=0, max_tokens=500, messages=[...])
Temperature 0 is not a guarantee of identical outputs across runs or model versions

chapters.title: System vs User Prompts
points: System prompt sets persistent role, rules, tone and output format; the user message carries the per-turn task and data
Put stable instructions in the system prompt so they apply to every turn and can be cached
Put untrusted content (user input, retrieved documents) in the user turn, fenced with delimiters like <context>...</context>
Instruction priority is a convention, not a security boundary: a system prompt can be leaked or overridden by prompt injection
Example: system = 'You are a support bot. Answer only from the provided context.' user = question plus <context> block
Mistake: pasting secrets or API keys into the system prompt, or burying critical rules at the end of a long user message

chapters.title: Structured Output with JSON Schemas
points: Structured output makes the model return machine-parseable JSON that matches a schema, so code can consume it without regex
A JSON Schema declares type, properties, required, enum and additionalProperties:false to constrain fields and values
Three levels of strength: prompt asks for JSON (weakest), JSON mode (valid JSON, any shape), schema-constrained or tool-call output (enforces the schema)
Example schema: {"type":"object","properties":{"sentiment":{"enum":["pos","neg","neu"]},"score":{"type":"number"}},"required":["sentiment","score"]}
Always validate the parsed result in code (Pydantic or Zod) and retry on failure; valid syntax does not mean correct values
Mistakes: forgetting required, using free-text fields where an enum fits, and letting max_tokens cut the JSON off mid-object

chapters.title: Grounding and RAG Prompt Templates
points: Hallucination happens because the model predicts plausible text from training patterns, not from verified facts; it has no built-in 'I don't know'
Grounding supplies retrieved passages in the prompt so the answer is drawn from given evidence instead of memory, reducing fabrication
RAG flow: embed the query, retrieve the top-k chunks, build the prompt with those chunks, then generate the answer
Template: system rules, then <context>{chunks}</context>, then the question; instruct 'answer only from the context, otherwise say you don't know'
Add source IDs to each chunk and require citations like [doc2] so answers can be checked
Mistakes: retrieving irrelevant or too many chunks (noise and lost-in-the-middle), no refusal instruction, and no check that the answer is supported by the context

chapters.title: Prompting Cheat Sheet
points: Tokens: about 4 chars each; window = input + output; count with the model's own tokenizer
Sampling: temperature 0 for factual and structured tasks, higher for creative; tune temperature or top-p, not both
Prompts: system = role, rules, format; user = task plus fenced untrusted data
Structured output: schema with required and enum, then validate and retry; never trust syntax alone
RAG template: rules, then <context> with source IDs, then question, with 'answer only from context or say you don't know'
